g.text: Log-rate transport on the true source subspace
Cross-assay transport in an exact-model simulation
Known source dimension | 3 independent worlds per dimension | 3 assays

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #444444

g.text: Each small point is one world; lines and horizontal bars show the median of three worlds. All selected fits are retained.

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #444444

g.text: Black crosses mark failure to meet the gradient criterion. Continuation has no total iteration cap; numerical failure can still stop it.

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #444444

g.text: Numerical convergence does not imply a global optimum. Estimation failure does not disprove the identifiability theorem.

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #444444

g.text: Favorable exact-model conditions and known dimension; only three replicates. This tests transport, not causal directions.

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #444444

g.text: The 10% line covers only the error criteria; full recovery also requires numerical and predictive checks. Vertical axes use logarithmic scales.
